solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Soldier dropped medal in front of a walled chapel

parts.note: a paratrooper is a soldier dropped from the air

explanation.surface: A soldier is stripped of his medal outside a fortified chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped' looks like a verb about losing the medal, but it belongs with the soldier: a para is dropped by parachute. BEM is the British Empire Medal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Byzantine church architecture this term names a side chapel separated from the main building by walls.

clue.text: One leading with several others favourite to clinch pole vault

indicators.note: to clinch is to grip tightly, so one piece holds another inside

parts.note: a vault is an arched roof

explanation.surface: The favourite expects to win the pole vault event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole vault' is a single athletics event in the surface, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a ruler is one of five governors sharing power jointly, so leads together with four colleagues.

clue.text: Parasitic larva touching a hand recoiled

indicators.note: recoiled means sprang back, so the letters go in reverse

parts.note: to give a hand is to aid

explanation.surface: A parasite brushes a hand, which jerks away.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a larval stage of a fluke, which develops inside a snail host before the next stage.

clue.text: Voracious herbivores out to lunch having change of heart in place of diet

indicators.note: a change of the following word means its letters are rearranged
having means holding within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the German city where the Diet of Worms condemned Luther in 1521

explanation.surface: Greedy eaters go out to lunch and, changing their minds, go on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' and 'diet' sound like eating habits; the diet is the Imperial assembly, and Worms is where it met.
explanation.definitionFit: These moth caterpillars travel in large groups devouring crops, so they are hungry plant-eaters.

clue.text: Other half of US pop duo kicking off meeting, standing in for French historian

parts.words: Other half of US pop duo
parts.note: the US phrase 'mom and pop': mom is pop's partner

indicators.note: kicking off means starting, so only the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: One half of an American pop duo, starting at a meeting, deputises for a French historian.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pop duo' is not a band: in American English 'mom and pop' pairs the parents, so the other half of pop is mom. 'French historian' is a false unit; Mommsen was German.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodor Mommsen was the German scholar who wrote a great History of Rome and won the Nobel Prize.

clue.text: Grade maybe acquired in part was unsuccessful

indicators.note: something acquired is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Lew Grade, the British TV and film mogul; 'maybe' flags the example

explanation.surface: A student's mark, partly earned, shows they failed.
explanation.walkthrough: Grade reads as a school mark; it is Lew Grade, the impresario who ran British commercial television.
explanation.definitionFit: To have failed at something is, in the colloquial phrase, to have made a mess of the chance.

clue.text: Dispersing around top of zone, this salty, acidy product of sewer

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap the single one
dispersing scatters the following letters into a new order
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Something salty and acidic spreads through a zone from the sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sewer is not a drain but one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: An embroidery stitch forming loops like petals, so it is something made by a person with needle and thread.

clue.text: What Asian restaurant-goers, first of all, try to break in two?

definitions.text: What Asian restaurant-goers, first of all, try to break in two?

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of every one of the preceding words

parts.note: opening letters of the three words

indicators.note: breaking in means getting inside, so a piece is placed within another

parts.note: to have a bash is to try

explanation.surface: What do diners in an Asian restaurant try to snap apart?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: these are disposable wooden chopsticks, joined at one end, that diners split before eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese disposable chopsticks come as one piece of wood that the diner pulls apart into a pair.

clue.text: Cheers fellow bringing Mexican dish

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A cheerful man brings out a Mexican meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' as a toast suggests drinks; here it means thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: This is seasoned meat in maize dough steamed inside a corn husk, a traditional food of Mexico.

clue.text: Newcastle team wanting leg up following mishit

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters climb, read from bottom to top
wanting means lacking, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: Newcastle Falcons, the rugby union club
the leg side in cricket is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A Newcastle side, lacking a leg-up after a miskick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg up' reads as a boost but splits: the leg goes, and up turns the rest over.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfing term for a bad stroke in which the club scrapes the ground before striking the ball.

clue.text: Unpleasant odour: one given off by composer repelled

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the remaining letters run the other way
what is given off leaves its source, so those letters are removed from the name

parts.note: one refers back to the definition: BO, body odour, is an unpleasant odour

explanation.surface: A bad smell wafts from a composer who keeps people away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the clever bit: it means one unpleasant odour, BO, which comes off the front of BORODIN, and what is left is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the smell of burning or cooking fat or meat, especially a strong disagreeable one.

clue.text: Prayer books border on strongly aggressive: an unknown number held

indicators.note: in an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y, so the first-named piece is sent second
something held is gripped inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: x, y and z are unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: Religious books verge on aggressive, with an unknown figure kept inside.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'border on X' puts the border after X.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Jewish festival prayer books used for the High Holy Days and other feasts, the Hebrew plural form.

clue.text: Compulsion to shift about — not that one should stop oddly alas

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug its gap, so these pieces go inside
oddly means take the letters in odd-numbered positions only

parts.note: first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A fidgety restlessness, and one person's lament that it should stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of the definition but supplies CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term describes restlessness and an inability to sit still, often a side effect of drugs.

clue.text: Best in combat, ball girl presented with bronze medal, finally

parts.note: a debutante is a girl presented at a ball

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words

parts.note: end letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A tennis ball girl is awarded third place in a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The ball is a dance, not a tennis ball: a deb is a young society woman making her debut.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb, in Milton, meaning to conquer or beat down an enemy in war.

clue.text: Bow, possibly, in presenting brilliant rock bands

definitions.note: clarain is a mass noun for the material forming the bands

parts.note: Clara Bow, the silent film star; 'possibly' flags the example

explanation.surface: A violin bow, perhaps, appears in a show by brilliant rock groups.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow suggests a violinist or an archer; it is the surname of Clara Bow, 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists use the name for the bright, glossy layers seen in banded bituminous coal.

clue.text: Firefighting management assisting officer outside house, displaying spirit

indicators.note: outside means on both sides of, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: aide-de-camp, an officer assisting a general

explanation.surface: A fire brigade's officer outside a burning house shows real spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Firefighting means tackling crises as they arise, not putting out fires.
explanation.definitionFit: This organisational style replaces fixed bureaucracy with improvised teams formed to handle each emerging crisis.

clue.text: Plea for truce, mostly weak, is coming from the Right

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
in an across clue, coming from the right means reading right to left

explanation.surface: A feeble political plea for a ceasefire comes from the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes it look political; it is just a direction. The phrase is old schoolchildren's slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic English playground slang called out to claim exemption or a pause in a game, like 'pax'.

clue.text: Plant bashful kiss, all atremble

indicators.note: trembling letters are shaken loose and settle in a new order

parts.note: x is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A shy person plants a nervous kiss, trembling all over.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealand flax, a tall fibrous perennial, is known by this name in its native country.

clue.text: Personification of fairness and belief in God advancing millions

indicators.note: advancing means moving forward, so this letter is taken out and set earlier in the word

explanation.surface: Fairness and faith together, with money pushing ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of THEISM moves two places forward.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology this Titaness embodies divine law, order and justice, usually shown with scales.

clue.text: In short, won't be going to Central Asia to see Chinese province

indicators.note: in short means cut short, so the last letter is lost
central asks for the middle letters only

explanation.surface: Someone briefly refuses a trip to Central Asia to visit a part of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central Asia' looks like a region but only means the middle of the word Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the older romanised spelling of Shanxi, a northern region of the People's Republic.

clue.text: Romantically sentimental book gorily re-plotted

indicators.note: a story re-plotted has its parts rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A soppy romance novel is rewritten as a gory one.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes stories built around courtship, hence sentimental and romantic in a juvenile way.

clue.text: Typical of man's error, guarding appearance half-heartedly

indicators.note: guarding means enclosing for protection, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder

indicators.note: half the heart goes, so one of the two central letters is dropped

explanation.surface: A man's blunder in keeping up appearances, half-hearted as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes stereotypically masculine behaviour, such as that of a bloke, a British term for a guy.

clue.text: Union no longer means to be heard more widely in Australia

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a microphone is a means to be heard more widely

explanation.surface: An Australian union has lost its way of getting its voice heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Amicus was a big British trade union, merged into Unite in 2007, hence 'no longer'.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a large British labour organisation that later merged with another to form the present body Unite.

clue.text: Party mostly backed article with colourful flyer

indicators.note: backed here means run backwards
mostly means not all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a camp is a party or faction

explanation.surface: A political party largely backs a newspaper piece accompanied by a bright leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a printed handbill; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This large tropical American parrot has vivid red, blue and yellow plumage, so it flies in bright colours.

clue.text: I note gold in a chest they open to let in water

definitions.text: they open to let in water

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the others

parts.note: seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone tucks a note and some gold into a chest that leaks.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sluice gates in Canadian dykes, with flaps that swing to control the passage of tidal water.

clue.text: Little Herb's handknit unravels, after spinning and shrinking

indicators.note: spinning turns the run of letters round to face the other way
shrinking leaves only a small inner part of the words

parts.note: letters from the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Little Herbert's hand-knitted jumper falls apart after spinning in the washer and shrinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb looks like a boy's name; it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This is another name for the earthnut or pignut, a small umbelliferous plant with an edible tuber.

clue.text: Doorman's chief time for fooling, taking in appropriate person?

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so a piece goes inside another

parts.note: a fool, the right sort of person for that day

explanation.surface: A head porter's day for practical jokes catches the right victim.
explanation.walkthrough: The date is written APR 1, with the 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: In India the word was used for an office messenger or orderly who stood at the door wearing a badge.

clue.text: Malay prince returning a huge fan of this country?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so everything is read in the opposite direction

parts.words: a huge fan of this country
parts.note: a nut is a fan; this country, for a Times setter, is the UK

explanation.surface: A royal comes home a great admirer of his host nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is used for a prince or high noble in Malaysia, as in Tunku Abdul Rahman.

clue.text: Old Nazi militia even seen around southern State in the past

indicators.note: seen around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

explanation.surface: Nazi Brownshirts were found even in a southern state long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a US state with southern; it is the verb 'say', in the old second-person form.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic form used with 'thou' means you declare or speak, as in older English and the Bible.

clue.text: Slaughter of woman impacted on a husband

explanation.surface: A woman's killing has had an effect on her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Jewish ritual method of killing animals for food so that the meat is kosher.
